lines.text: Part_Desc: 578806 Festool Delta S GR PRO/10

attributes.name: Form
attributes.description: The physical format the abrasive is supplied in, which determines what machine holds it. A belt and a disc of identical grain and grit fit nothing in common, so this is the first thing a buyer filters on.

attributes.name: Grit
attributes.description: Grit designation exactly as the supplier writes it, including the scale prefix. Recorded as a string on purpose: P150 (FEPA) and 150 (ANSI/CAMI) are different specifications above roughly P220, so storing a bare number would equate two products that are not equivalent.

attributes.name: Size
attributes.description: The manufacturer's headline size statement, kept as published with its axis labels intact, e.g. "24 in W x 24-1/4 in D". Deliberately a string and not a dimension_set: the published form varies in both the number of axes and their order, and the client's ground truth carries no unit column for it, so reformatting into a fixed W x H x D triple would discard information and diverge from the expected output.

attributes.name: Nominal Length
attributes.description: Overall length as the manufacturer designates it, for tubes, strips and linear fixtures. A designation rather than a measurement: a nominal 4' fluorescent tube is 47-3/4" so that it fits a 4' fixture, and recording the measured figure would contradict every catalogue.

attributes.name: Diameter
attributes.description: Outside diameter of a wheel, disc or pad. This is the figure the machine's guard limits, so a larger wheel is never a substitute for a smaller one even though it removes more.

attributes.name: Abrasive Grain
attributes.description: The mineral doing the cutting. Grain choice is matched to the workpiece rather than to the operation: zirconia and ceramic hold an edge on steel where aluminium oxide dulls, and silicon carbide is for masonry and non-ferrous work where the others glaze.

attributes.name: Backing
attributes.description: The flexible substrate a coated abrasive's grain is bonded to. Governs how far the product conforms to a contour and whether it survives wet use, which is why the same grain and grit on film and on paper are not interchangeable.

attributes.name: Attachment
attributes.description: How the abrasive fixes to its backing pad or machine. A mismatch here is a hard stop even when diameter and grit are right, so it is recorded separately from the arbor.

attributes.name: Operation
attributes.description: The material-removal operation the product is built for. Cutting wheels are thin and loaded radially; grinding wheels are thick and loaded on the face. Using one for the other is a safety matter rather than a preference, which is why a dual-rated product is its own value instead of being recorded as both.

allowed_values.note: dual-rated wheel; thickness is a compromise between the two duties

attributes.name: Material Application
attributes.description: The materials the product is intended to be used on. Multivalued because a single wheel is commonly rated for several, and reporting only the first would understate what the buyer can do with it.

attributes.name: Product Series
attributes.description: Manufacturer's series or family designation only, without the word "series" and without the manufacturer name. The anchor for part-number grammar induction, because the positional encoding of a smart part number is defined per series rather than per manufacturer.

attributes.name: Pack Quantity
attributes.description: Number of units in the consumer pack the part number sells as. Distinct from case_quantity, which counts packs in a shipping carton: a "3pk" of lamps is one sellable unit containing three lamps, and confusing the two misprices the line.

attributes.name: Selling Unit of Measure
attributes.description: The unit in which the product is sold, which is not necessarily the unit in which it is priced or stocked. Conflating the three is a classic source of order errors.

attributes.name: Carton Quantity
attributes.description: Number of selling units per carton or master pack for this specific part number. Frequently varies by size within one series, so read the ordering-table row that matches the target SKU.

attributes.name: Additional Information
attributes.description: Comma-separated residual specifications the class has no dedicated attribute for, in the client's own overflow convention, e.g. "240 kW-hr Annual Energy, 1 to 12 hr Delay Start Hours". A holding pen, not a dumping ground: anything appearing here repeatedly across a category is a missing attribute and should be promoted to one.
example_values: 240 kW-hr Annual Energy, 1 to 12 hr Delay Start Hours
Folding Tines, Leak Detection System, Normal Cycle

attributes.name: Approvals and Listings
attributes.description: Third-party certifications, listings and approvals explicitly stated in the source. Record only what is stated. A listing number without a recognised mark is not an approval, and an approval for one size in a series does not extend to the others.

allowed_values.note: Generic NSF mark with no standard named. Deliberately not aliased onto NSF-61: a potable-water claim needs the specific standard, and treating this as equivalent would let a cross-field rule pass on evidence that does not support it.
eye and face protection impact rating
hand protection cut, abrasion and puncture rating
building-code evaluation report for a structural or envelope product
composite decking and railing performance standard

attributes.name: Country of Origin
attributes.description: Country where the product is manufactured, as stated by the manufacturer. Drives tariff treatment and trade-agreement eligibility, so a guess here has direct financial consequences.

attributes.name: California Prop 65 Warning Required
attributes.description: True when the source states that a California Proposition 65 warning applies. Absence of a statement is not evidence of absence of a requirement, so record a gap rather than false when the source is silent.

attributes.name: GTIN / UPC
attributes.description: Global Trade Item Number, 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits. The final digit is a modulo-10 check digit, which L0 validation verifies arithmetically — a transposed digit is therefore detectable without any external lookup.

cross_field_rules.message: A diameter was recorded against a belt, which has none. Belt dimensions are width by length and wheel dimensions are diameter by thickness, so this means a two-figure belt size was read with the three-figure wheel convention.

Coated abrasives are almost always sold in multiples and the count is stated as a bare "6pc" or "50 Disc/Box" that sits beside real dimensions. A pack quantity below one means a dimension was captured instead of the count.
